thread:
sophia (EDR-bot): [ALERT] Suspicious service chain observed on host john-d-mbp (hostid: hb-9a3f). Parent: /usr/local/bin/launcher -> child: /usr/bin/ms-updater (unsigned). Network beacon to 3rd-party IPs. Quarantine suggested.
jamie (secops): Confirming. @alex can you isolate the device from network and push an endpoint quarantine? Please also collect the EDR trace.
alex (it-support): On it. Pushed isolation (~10s). Running remote collection now.
alex (it-support): Command used: ```edrctl isolate --host hb-9a3f && edrctl collect --host hb-9a3f --type process-tree,net-conns,files``` will upload to secure bucket.
leo (oncall): Noted. User john.d is online and says they were on a client call earlier. @john.d please disconnect from wifi and avoid using any corporate creds until we confirm.
john.d (employee): ack, disconnecting now. I didn't click anything strange but saw a dialog "Updater needs permission" earlier.
jamie (secops): Good. @matt can you check if this svc chain matches any current rollout artifacts? Could be a mis-signed helper from a 3rd party tool.
matt (eng): Checking release artifacts... nothing matches /usr/bin/ms-updater name. No rollout with that binary. It looks foreign.
sophia (EDR-bot): Scan result: found file /usr/local/bin/launcher (sha256: c3a9f...7b) — suspicious persistence (launchd plist modified). Child process spawned with TLS cert pinned to unknown host. C2 domains: bad.example.net, 45.77.12.99.
jamie (secops): Ok escalate to forensics. @forensics-team take the collected artifacts (s3://redwood-sec/collections/hb-9a3f/) and start triage. Preserve disk image if needed.
forensics-team: We'll start live triage and schedule a disk snap. ETA 30m for initial triage. We'll also dump browser artifacts and inspect the launchd plist.
jamie (secops): Action items: 1) Contain device (done) 2) Collect artifacts (done) 3) Block C2 IPs and domains at network level (leo) 4) Check KMS audit logs for any suspicious key access for john.d's identity or service account usage (matt) 5) Rotate any service creds if found.
leo (oncall): Blocking IPs/domains at edge and WAF now. Added firewall rules: drop to 45.77.12.99/32 and null-route bad.example.net.
matt (eng): KMS/secret manager: I'm tailing audit logs for the last 48h for principal john.d and hostid hb-9a3f. No KMS Decrypt operations from that host so far. Will continue monitoring.
jamie (secops): Good. Also add RBAC note: limit ephemeral dev tool tokens — we saw the launcher invoked with elevated token in process args (redacted). Create incident ticket to review token scopes.
alex (it-support): Looping in user manager and MDM: pushing a full disk scan and pending OS update. Will schedule swap if disk image shows compromise.
john.d (employee): Thanks everyone. Anything I should change passwords for now?
jamie (secops): For now rotate any high-priv tokens you used during the day (ssh keys, cloud console). We'll confirm whether creds were exfiltrated. Please don't reuse old passwords.
forensics-team: Initial triage: launcher is a dropper; launchd plist persists in ~/Library/LaunchAgents with unusual run-at-load and curl command. Dropped binary is obfuscated. We'll escalate to malware analysis.
jamie (secops): We'll need a short incident slack comms and an entry in the incident channel summarizing containment and next steps. Assigning incident lead: jamie.
leo (oncall): I've added incident channel #incident-2123456789 and posted a quick heads-up to infra and legal.
jamie (secops): Postmortem owners: secops+eng+it. Also request a follow-up audit on audit-logging pipeline to ensure no gaps in EDR event ingestion for that time window.
forensics-team: Malware analysis ETA 4-6 hours. If confirmed exfiltration, start credential rotation plan and check for lateral movement.
jamie (secops): Thanks. Closing loop for now — we'll update thread as artifacts arrive. :lock: :mag:
